name: D-2 Student visa (degree-seeking)

requirements.blocker_text: Requires admission to an accredited associate, bachelor's, master's, or doctoral degree program at a Korean university (D-4 covers non-degree language institutes and vocational training instead).
requirements.fix_path: Secure admission to an accredited Korean degree program.

requirements.blocker_text: Requires proof of sufficient financial means (bank balance certificate, scholarship award, or sponsor's financial guarantee) covering tuition and living costs.
requirements.fix_path: Provide bank statements, a scholarship award letter, or a sponsor's financial guarantee.

evidence_required.document: Certificate of admission from the Korean institution
Bank balance certificate or scholarship documentation
Alien Registration Card (ARC) application within 90 days of arrival for stays over 90 days

outcome.duration_length: tied to program length, renewed periodically via ARC

sources.title: HiKorea -- Korea Immigration Service's official portal for visa categories, ARC, and stay procedures

notes: D-2 holders may work part-time only with explicit, separately-obtained permission for activities outside their status of residence -- general unrestricted part-time work is not permitted, and this permission must be obtained before working, not after. Standard graduation pathway: D-2 holders convert to D-10 (job-seeker) status after graduating rather than working immediately, using the D-10 period to secure the specific employer sponsorship an E-7 (or, for the small number of qualifying strategic-industry fields, E-7-T under the Top-Tier Visa track effective April 2025) requires -- this D-2 to D-10 to E-7 sequence is the standard route Korea's own immigration-service guidance and independent secondary sources describe consistently for foreign graduates, distinct from the direct-to-employment pattern seen in some other countries' student routes in this dataset. The Top-Tier Visa track (8 strategic industries: AI, semiconductors, displays, secondary batteries, biotech, advanced mobility, robotics, defense) offers graduates in those specific fields a D-10-T to E-7-T to F-2-T to F-5-T pathway with different income and credential rules than the standard track -- not separately modeled as its own route file given its current narrow scope, but flagged here since it changes this route's most likely next step for STEM/strategic-industry graduates specifically.
